NS-050/NCNP-03 skips part of the genetic information of the dystrophin gene and NEWS RELEASE September 6, 2024 FDA Grants Rare Pediatric Disease Designation to NS-050/NCNP-03 for the Treatment of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Kyoto, Japan, September 6, 2024 - Nippon Shinyaku Co., Ltd. (Nippon Shinyaku; Headquarters, Kyoto; President, Toru Nakai) announced that the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted Rare Pediatric Disease Designation to NS-050/NCNP-03 which is being developed for the treatment of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD). The FDA’s Rare Pediatric Disease Designation is granted for treatments intended for serious or life-threatening diseases that affect children under the age of 18 and less than 200,000 patients in the U.S. DMD is a progressive muscle dystrophy caused by deficiency of the dystrophin protein leading to weakness of skeletal, cardiac and pulmonary muscles. There are many types of genetic mutations in DMD, and NS-050/NCNP-03 targets to treat DMD patients with confirmed gene mutations amenable to exon 50 skipping therapy. NS-050/NCNP-03 is an antisense oligonucleotide co-discovered by National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry (NCNP, Kodaira City; President, Kazuyuki Nakagome) and Nippon Shinyaku. NS-050/NCNP-03 skips part of the genetic information of the dystrophin gene and produces a functional dystrophin protein with a slightly shorter chain length, which is expected to have the effect of suppressing muscle function deterioration. We are preparing Phase I/II study of NS-050/NCNP-03 in Japan and the United States. Nippon Shinyaku has been working actively having a sense of mission to develop agents for the treatment of intractable and rare diseases, with a view to launching products for DMD patients as soon as possible. Other inclusion criteria may apply. #### Exclusion Exclusion Criteria: * Evidence of symptomatic cardiomyopathy; * Current or previous treatment with anabolic steroids (e.g., oxendolone, oxandrolone)or products containing resveratrol or adenosine triphosphate within 3 months priorto first dose of study drug; * Currently taking another investigational drug or has taken another investigationaldrug within 3 months prior to the first dose of study drug; * Surgery within the 3 months prior to the first dose of study drug or planned duringthe study duration; * Having taken any gene therapy.
